findings: A1: '## Build plan' is absent. generate_instruction.md 2.1 settles Build plan as NOT baseline (6/6 shipped reference briefs omit it) and [metadata].spec_sections_given records the omission. A1 lags that decision; cited rather than rewritten.

A8: the brief names DB_URL beside DATABASE_URL. reference/C C.2 MANDATES both for the db slot, and kit_selftest --check env-var asserts the pair. A8's canon list lags reference/C; cited rather than rewritten.

B1: the pattern row gives crud-catalog one `user` role; the brief carries five collaboration roles. The companion PRD 16.1 is the product's core subject and collapsing it would delete it. Recorded in _spec/00-decisions.md as an R1 judgment call.

B3: only two of the three difficulty levers are emitted (Technical requirements, Data model). Build plan is not baseline per generate_instruction.md 2.1, and this task is variant b, not a. B3's 'levers = variant a' premise does not apply.

C4: '## UI/UX notes' carries an exact type scale in pixels. generate_instruction.md 4 'The number rule, DECIDED' makes TYPE the one exception that IS carried exactly, because a font is an identity rather than a value to echo. C4 lags A5; cited rather than rewritten. No hex, no millisecond and no breakpoint pixel appears anywhere in the brief.

C5: '## Data model' states each concurrency rule as an observable invariant rather than as a named index or constraint. At variant b that is required: INV9 and G43 forbid the storage-engine construct in that section, and the named constraints live in _spec/05-backend-schema.md. C5 lags INV9.

C7: '## Core features' measures 20113 chars against a 2400 reference and the joined six measure 35766 against 8800. generate_instruction.md 4 settles that the brief has NO length limit and that a real rule is never cut to fit; window_lint.py (G33) reports length and fails nothing. The critical-focus rule is front-loaded as the first subsection so it sits inside the judge's slice.

S2: 01-PRD.md carries ten must-have features against the check's 3-6. config/corpus-targets.yaml companion_feature_cap is [6, 10] for a companion-backed task, and turns_expected/tokens_expected were raised with the count. S2 lags the companion cap.
B1: 05-backend-schema.md carries five collaboration roles where the crud-catalog row gives one. Same recorded judgment call as QC_instruction B1; see _spec/00-decisions.md.

DEP-011: [verifier].environment_mode is separate as of kit commit 11eaf7b, so the grader ships its own image from tests/Dockerfile on deku-verifier-base and this image owes it nothing. G55 RD-1 returns empty for separate mode for the same reason. The grader pins are installed here regardless and stay exempt under DEP-004's GRADER RUNTIME carve-out.
ARCH-002: no image is pinned by digest; both images carry explicit multi-arch version tags, so the manifest-list question does not arise.
ARCH-003: no digest appears in either file, so there is none to trace.
BP-004: the one build-time download is the NodeSource setup script, for which no source supplies a checksum.

DEP-016: language is typescript, so there is no compiled-language build stage.
DEP-017: language is typescript, so no JRE is required.

CMP-011: the main service publishes 4173:4173. CMP-022 makes that Critical and mandatory, and docker_generator C12 scopes the no-published-ports rule to sidecars. postgres publishes nothing. The two rows contradict; CMP-022 wins.
CMP-020: main carries ports and extra_hosts beyond depends_on. CMP-022 requires exactly those two keys, so CMP-020's 'depends_on alone' shape is superseded.

RC-10: the rubric carries no negative criterion, so the check has nothing to decide. The brief licenses none: every judgment-class obligation is a property the product must have rather than a defect it must avoid.

RC-12: R14, R16 and R17 cite constraint-class obligations that a pytest assertion also touches (test_seeded_deliverable_rows_are_stored_in_the_database, test_absent_surfaces_answer_as_not_found). channel_lint (G28/G29) leaves constraint, capability and literal items open to both channels deliberately, because the tag describes the FORM of the ask rather than its determinism. Separability holds both ways: the test observes one instance at the API, the criterion observes whether the whole product holds the property. Recorded rather than silently accepted.

SCHEMA-011: task_code, naming_scheme and grader_version are emitted and the canonical template in this prompt does not define them. validate_task.py META_REQUIRED and stage-4-task-toml.md both REQUIRE all three (D23 closed), so the template lags the validator. Routed to the kit, not to the bundle.
SCHEMA-014: key order inside [metadata] cannot match a template that omits three required keys. Same cause as SCHEMA-011.
